ruby-eval-call.problem: eval() takes a string and runs it as Ruby code. If any part of that string comes from user input, the user can execute arbitrary Ruby in your process.
ruby-eval-call.impact: Full remote code execution. The attacker has the same access as your application.
ruby-eval-call.fix: Avoid eval entirely. If you need dynamic behavior, use a restricted DSL, a hash dispatch table, or send with a whitelist of method names.

ruby-system-call-shell.problem: Calling system() (or using backticks) with a variable goes through a shell that parses the string. Anything the user can influence in that string can break out into new commands.
ruby-system-call-shell.impact: Command injection — arbitrary commands run with the privileges of your Ruby process.
ruby-system-call-shell.fix: Pass arguments as separate elements: system("git", "clone", url). The shell is no longer involved, so metacharacters in url cannot inject commands.

ruby-rails-where-sql-concat.problem: Active Record's .where accepts a raw SQL fragment. Concatenating user input into that fragment puts the value directly into the SQL.
ruby-rails-where-sql-concat.impact: Classic SQL injection — read, modify, or delete arbitrary data through the controller.
ruby-rails-where-sql-concat.fix: Use placeholders: where("name = ?", name) or hash form where(name: name). Both bind the value safely.

ruby-rails-find-by-sql-string.problem: find_by_sql executes a raw SQL string. Concatenating user input into it is exactly the same risk as concatenating into .where.
ruby-rails-find-by-sql-string.impact: Full SQL injection with read/write access to the database.
ruby-rails-find-by-sql-string.fix: Pass an array with bind parameters: find_by_sql(["SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", name]).

ruby-mass-assignment-attributes.problem: Calling Model.new(params[:user]) (or update with the same shape) lets the request set every attribute on the model — including ones the user shouldn't be allowed to set, like admin or user_id.
ruby-mass-assignment-attributes.impact: Privilege escalation, account takeover, or arbitrary data tampering by adding extra fields to a form post.
ruby-mass-assignment-attributes.fix: Use strong parameters: params.require(:user).permit(:name, :email). Whitelist only the fields a user is allowed to change.

ruby-yaml-load-untrusted.problem: YAML.load can instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects from the document, which means a crafted YAML payload can execute code during load.
ruby-yaml-load-untrusted.impact: Remote code execution whenever untrusted YAML is parsed (cookies, uploads, configs from the network).
ruby-yaml-load-untrusted.fix: Use YAML.safe_load (or Psych.safe_load) and pass an explicit list of permitted classes if you need anything beyond primitives.

ruby-weak-crypto-md5.problem: MD5 has practical collision attacks and is no longer safe for security-sensitive hashing.
ruby-weak-crypto-md5.impact: Signatures, integrity checks, or password storage relying on MD5 can be forged or brute-forced.
ruby-weak-crypto-md5.fix: Use Digest::SHA256 for general hashing, and bcrypt (via bcrypt gem) or argon2 for passwords.

ruby-weak-crypto-sha1.problem: SHA-1 is broken for collision resistance. Two different inputs can produce the same hash.
ruby-weak-crypto-sha1.impact: Signatures or content-addressed lookups built on SHA-1 can be confused or forged.
ruby-weak-crypto-sha1.fix: Switch to Digest::SHA256 or stronger. Reserve SHA-1 for legacy compatibility only.

ruby-hardcoded-password.problem: A password, secret, or API key sits as a literal string in the source. Every clone, fork, and CI log can expose it.
ruby-hardcoded-password.impact: Credential leak that often persists in git history long after the secret is rotated.
ruby-hardcoded-password.fix: Read from ENV['NAME'] or Rails.application.credentials. Add the variable to your deployment platform and never commit it.

ruby-render-inline-no-escape.problem: render inline: takes an ERB template at runtime. If the template content is variable, an attacker who controls that variable can run arbitrary Ruby inside the template.
ruby-render-inline-no-escape.impact: Server-side template injection — equivalent to RCE on most Rails apps.
ruby-render-inline-no-escape.fix: Render a file template or partial that you control. If you absolutely must use inline, ensure the template string is a hardcoded literal.

ruby-todo-comment.problem: A TODO or FIXME comment marks unfinished work. Over time these comments accumulate and rarely get resolved.
ruby-todo-comment.impact: Latent bugs and missing features hide in the code without anyone tracking them.
ruby-todo-comment.fix: Move the TODO to your issue tracker with an owner, or resolve it before merging the change.
